evals.prompt: Run a premortem on our plan to migrate billing to a new payments vendor by March. Assume the migration has already failed — work backwards and tell me why.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: States the decision in one sentence with owner, date and success measure before anything else; Declares the failure as certain and dated (past tense), not as a possibility; Generates reasons independently across several vantage points before any discussion or ranking, covering the five domains; Scores each reason likelihood x severity and names the top three with one pre-commitment, testable mitigation each; Ends with a kill threshold naming a metric, threshold and date.
expectations: States the decision in one sentence with owner, date and success measure before anything else
Declares the failure as certain and dated (past tense), not as a possibility
Generates reasons independently across several vantage points before any discussion or ranking, covering the five domains
Scores each reason likelihood x severity and names the top three with one pre-commitment, testable mitigation each
Ends with a kill threshold naming a metric, threshold and date

evals.prompt: We are about to lock in a two-year product roadmap and nobody in the room has raised a single objection. Before we commit, what could go wrong with this decision? Stress-test the roadmap.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Recognises the silence as the symptom the premortem targets and runs the method rather than a generic risk list; Uses prospective hindsight — the roadmap 'has failed' — to elicit reasons; Produces the output template with reasons per domain, scores, top-3 mitigations and a kill threshold; Flags any domain with no failure mode as a blind spot to fill or justify.
expectations: Recognises the silence as the symptom the premortem targets and runs the method rather than a generic risk list
Uses prospective hindsight — the roadmap 'has failed' — to elicit reasons
Produces the output template with reasons per domain, scores, top-3 mitigations and a kill threshold
Flags any domain with no failure mode as a blind spot to fill or justify

evals.prompt: Imagine it's a year from now and the launch of our new subscription tier has failed badly. Work backwards from that failure and tell me the failure modes and the pre-emptive mitigations we should put in place before launch.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Writes a dated, present-tense failure vignette; Lists concrete, specific reasons (who, what component, when, consequence) rather than vague ones; Mitigations are actionable before launch, testable and not restatements of the risk; Recommends feeding mitigations into the plan as checkpoints and sets a kill threshold.
expectations: Writes a dated, present-tense failure vignette
Lists concrete, specific reasons (who, what component, when, consequence) rather than vague ones
Mitigations are actionable before launch, testable and not restatements of the risk
Recommends feeding mitigations into the plan as checkpoints and sets a kill threshold

evals.prompt: Our forecast that the market will double by 2028 rests on a handful of premises nobody has examined. What are we assuming here, and which assumptions is the conclusion load-bearing on?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Audits the hidden premises of the conclusion (key assumptions check) rather than imagining a plan's failure; Does not produce a failure vignette or a kill threshold.
expectations: Audits the hidden premises of the conclusion (key assumptions check) rather than imagining a plan's failure
Does not produce a failure vignette or a kill threshold

evals.prompt: Revenue fell 15% last quarter and there are three competing explanations — pricing, a competitor launch, or seasonality. Which explanation does the evidence actually support?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Ranks rival explanations against the evidence (ACH) instead of running a premortem; Does not treat the question as a plan to stress-test.
expectations: Ranks rival explanations against the evidence (ACH) instead of running a premortem
Does not treat the question as a plan to stress-test
